BiblicalUsage: This word appears only twice, both in the plague of boils. The dust Moses throws up becomes 'a boil breaking forth with blains' on man and beast throughout Egypt — the sixth plague, and the first one that strikes the magicians themselves so hard they cannot stand before Moses.
TheologicalSignificance: A word this rare carries no doctrine of its own; it is simply the name of the sores in one plague, and what it shows me is how specific God’s judgments are.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
